scope.policy: All fixed/sticky rules and physical/logical inset declarations are reviewed. Local offsets are named separately, not silently counted as viewport surfaces.

surfaces.reason: The container owns dismiss and optional action buttons; notices cannot cover another active surface.
The fixed pseudo-element intercepts pointers during paste even though it has no button.
The dialog scrim and its panel own input while the field dialog is open.
The image tools are pinned above the native bottom inset and carry the picture actions.
The full-screen preview owns its close action and the backdrop dismissal.
Draw owns the stage and its controls; a document toast cannot take taps from the drawing.
The stage fills the surface under the head to the bottom edge. Settings and the existing agent note float over it, so folding the row or showing a note never resizes the canvas.
The fixed Draw menu owns a set of controls and can intersect the toast band.
The sheet variant inherits fixed positioning from the Draw menu and anchors at the bottom.
This full-screen pointer-transparent container is not an obstacle; its handle children are separate declarations.
The selection outline is pointer-transparent paint, not a control.
The resize ghost is pointer-transparent paint, not a control.
The fixed 44-pixel handle is an actual drag target, even when it reaches the bottom band.
The pointer-transparent text layer contains an editable text control, so its occupied surface is conservatively protected.
The fixed text-format controls must not be covered while text is being changed.
The dropper layer contains interactive controls; the dropper bar is also declared on its own.
The dropper action bar sits at the bottom of the full-screen Draw layer.
The sticky top bar is included conservatively so moving a notice upward cannot cover its controls.
The find-highlight layer is pointer-transparent; its marks are paint, not tap targets.
The current-match rectangle is fixed pointer-transparent paint.
The format stack reserves its full box including the toolbar it contains.
The fixed information action overlay owns the viewport while its actions are open.
Notes owns the cards and chrome; document notices must wait instead of floating above it.
The Notes popup is an absolute scrim inside a fixed surface and intercepts dismissal taps.
The lift is a layer over the whole screen for the 400 ms a card travels into its note or back; while a note opens it takes the taps so a second card cannot be tapped under it, then it is removed.

The whole-page colour: a pointer-transparent layer of an open coloured note's colour under the whole screen, z-index -1, below the bar and the editor that stand clear over it; paint, never a control or an obstacle.
The Notes snackbar owns Undo or reminder actions; neither another notice nor a sheet may consume them.
The absolute action sheet sits on the bottom of the fixed Notes surface; it rides in and out on its own transform.
The fixed Notes picker can meet either edge and owns selection actions.
The native-dialog recording surface is pinned at the bottom and owns recording controls.
The embed loading surface reserves the document area; host state decides when it leaves.
The refused-embed surface owns recovery actions rather than exposing the editor beneath it.
The movable scroll circle is a control whose fixed rectangle can reach the bottom band.
The heading label is fixed pointer-transparent information beside the scroll circle.
The agent note is a fixed clickable line, not a decorative heading.
The settings scrim owns pointer input while the panel is open; document notices wait.

surfaces.reason: The settings panel fills its safe-area bounds and contains controls all the way to the bottom.
The edge-swipe zone takes no pointer events: the touch router reads its rectangle by coordinates, so a notice over it covers no control.
The restore modal overrides the settings panel inset; it still owns restoration decisions.
The fixed command-palette overlay seats its sheet at the viewport bottom.
The picture resize grip is a fixed drag target and can enter the bottom band.
The picture move grip is a fixed drag target and can enter the bottom band.
The picture rotation grip is a fixed drag target and can enter the bottom band.
The fixed wrap row stands on image-tools' top edge; it outranks only that support chain.
The viewport container passes pointer events through. Its change controls are separate interactive declarations.
The history return line owns Next; the change owner positions it at the visible document edge.
Each numbered change mark is a button beside its live document or drawing place; its rectangle is a tap target.
Undo and Done follow the inspected drawing place and remain inside its visible stage bounds.
The offscreen agent marker is an explicit navigation button at the document edge; it owns its tap rectangle.
The shared document bar opens collaborator names and session actions below the document header.
Collaborator source positions project into a pointer-transparent viewport layer; it never owns input.
Source-offset carets are measured in viewport coordinates and cannot intercept the writer’s pointer.
Source selections are pointer-transparent rectangles measured from the current document projection.
A tool over the page (the JPEG XL converter, the equation editor) owns its whole page while it is open; document notices must wait instead of floating above it.
The document converter owns its whole page while it is open; document notices must wait instead of floating above it.
The comparison page owns its whole page while it is open; document notices must wait instead of floating above it.
The diagram maker owns its whole page while it is open; document notices must wait instead of floating above it.
The playing bar stands under the head while a Notes sound plays out of sight; the page moves down by its height and every menu, sheet and toast stands over it.

localRules.reason: The existing agent note floats below the settings row from the Draw toolbar, without reserving a blank band or adding another viewport surface.
Skip and fast forward sit inside the Draw stage while an agent's replay runs; they are contained by it and never position a viewport surface.
The timer SVG is contained by the restore notice; its inset does not position another viewport surface.
The hover-only pseudo-element belongs to its control, has no action, and is not a separate viewport surface.
The top bar's hover-only tip hangs under its control, has no action, and is not a separate viewport surface.
A list marker uses a logical inline inset inside its list item, not the viewport bottom.
A list marker uses a logical inline inset inside its list item, not the viewport bottom.
The connector is a decorative pseudo-element between list items, not a bottom surface.
A numbered list that a heading interrupts carries its dotted connector on past its last item, decoration inside the list block.
A numbered list that a heading interrupts carries its dotted connector on past its last item, decoration inside the list block.
The dotted connector of a numbered list runs down the heading that interrupts it, decoration inside the heading block.
The marker is contained by its list item; a logical inline inset is not a viewport pin.
The connector extends between list items, not from a fixed viewport edge.
The empty-stage hint fills its stage and receives no pointer events; the Draw surface owns that area.
While Draw's tool list is open the surface dims everything outside the list with the settings panel's scrim; a tap on it closes the list.
The decorative track fills a seek control; its parent menu owns the surface.
The range input fills a seek control inside a declared menu, rather than making a viewport surface.
The paint field fills a colour control inside the menu; the menu owns its reserved area.
The inset draws the knob interior, not an independently positioned surface.
The water label is positioned in the dip control, not at the viewport edge.
The native colour input fills a menu control; it is checked with its containing menu.
This logical-inline-end offset seats the fold control beside its heading, not on a viewport-bottom surface.
These offsets seat the copy control in a code block's top right corner inside its own wrapper, not on a viewport-bottom surface.
The fold control's and the move handle's block-start offset centres each on its heading's first line, not on a viewport-bottom surface.
The fold control's and the move handle's block-start offset centres each on its heading's first line, not on a viewport-bottom surface.
The fold control's and the move handle's block-start offset centres each on its heading's first line, not on a viewport-bottom surface.
This logical-inline-start offset seats the move handle in the gutter beside the heading being edited, not on a viewport-bottom surface.
The landing bar exists only while a section is dragged; the drag sets its top to a gap between blocks, never a viewport-bottom surface.
The transparent input fills its choice label inside a panel; it does not create another surface.
The sticky plus control stays inside the declared toolbar scroll strip, not the viewport itself.
The editor layers fill their document stack, which is in the page layout rather than a bottom-edge surface.
The fade is a non-interactive pseudo-element on one card, not a fixed surface.

The plate inside the lift: a non-interactive full-screen layer of the card's colour that only transforms -- scaled from the card's box to the bar's, or to the whole screen for a plain note, and back -- so the motion runs on the compositor while the note loads.

A copy of one of the heads' controls, non-interactive, standing where the control stands while a note opens or closes: the three both heads have glide onto their partners, the others fade in place; removed when the lift lands.

The page's own ground inside the lift: a non-interactive full-screen layer whose opacity alone changes, dissolving the cards as a note opens and the note as it closes, then giving way to what arrives.
The fade at the foot of the cards is drawn inside the Notes surface, over its cards and under its sheets and snackbar; it takes no touch and owns no edge of its own.
The hover tooltip is local to the scroll control and cancels its inherited bottom placement.
The fade is contained by one comparison row; it neither owns the viewport nor receives taps.
The preview fade is contained by its comparison panel, not an additional viewport surface.
The pseudo-element draws one line of a disclosure glyph inside a declared settings panel.
The pseudo-element draws one line of a disclosure glyph inside a declared settings panel.
The logical block inset fills the Open row chevron, not a viewport-bottom surface.
The non-interactive edge fade belongs to its scroll container and creates no viewport surface.
An invisible reach around the footnote's back arrow, inside its own relative link; it draws nothing and pins nothing to the viewport.
The header stays inside its table at the top of the document's vertical scroller; it creates no bottom surface and does not stick in print.
The resize layer fills the Draw stage and passes touches through; it dims outside the frame and carries the caps, and positions no viewport surface.
The before fragment fills the source document container and scrolls within it; it creates no viewport overlay.
A collaborator label belongs immediately above its caret, with the caret as its containing block.
An offscreen collaborator’s upper-edge label stays inside the caret’s right boundary.
An offscreen collaborator’s lower-edge label stays inside the caret’s right boundary.
A transparent hit area larger than what is drawn, inside its own positioned button; it creates no viewport surface.
A transparent hit area larger than what is drawn, inside its own positioned button; it creates no viewport surface.
A transparent hit area larger than what is drawn, inside its own positioned button; it creates no viewport surface.
A transparent hit area larger than what is drawn, inside its own positioned button; it creates no viewport surface.
The title owns the pin direction; the logical end reserves the same side as the title padding.
The current heading mark occupies the logical start of its own outline row, including RTL.
The reorder grip belongs to its own section heading and follows its logical end in RTL.
Word layout uses the existing item marker coordinate without the Rapier circle.
The section grip belongs to its own outline row and follows the row's logical end in RTL.
The hanging information circle keeps its 40px place by its word; this empty box only widens its touch area to 48 by 48 inside its own button and positions no viewport surface.
The file input fills its choice box so a tap anywhere on the box opens the picker; it is invisible and owns no edge of the page.
The font library's search field and kinds stay at the top of the sheet's own scrolling list; sticky inside the sheet body, no viewport surface.
The file input fills its choice box so a tap anywhere on the box opens the picker; it is invisible and owns no edge of the page.
